This session visually inspected every one of those 10 files directly (not by filename).

usable_real_work_photos.description: Real: a man installing wood crown molding / trim with a nail gun in an interior room, standing on a ladder next to a window AC unit. Plausible handyman carpentry work.
Real: an open wall cavity showing exposed copper and PVC plumbing stubs behind a cut-out in a blue-painted wall, consistent with a plumbing/drywall repair job.

Borderline: a finished white sliding closet door unit with new base drawers in a hallway. Could be a finished carpentry job, but is generic enough that it cannot be confirmed as this business's own work with full confidence.

discarded_unrelated_or_contaminated.description: A sunset photo over a lake/fountain on what looks like a university campus (FIU-style building). No connection to handyman work.
A wall sign for 'Banfield, The Pet Hospital of Boca Raton, since 1955'. Completely unrelated business/location.
A pile of burned/discarded debris and a shopping cart in a parking lot. No identifiable connection to this business.
Interior shelving of what looks like a video game / DVD resale shop. Unrelated.
Same Banfield Pet Hospital Boca Raton wall sign, this time with a man on a scissor lift installing it. Unrelated business/location.
A 'Pet Training' sign-up kiosk inside what looks like a PetSmart-type pet supply store. Unrelated.
Dim, low-quality photo of shelving stacked with DVD/VHS-style cases in a dark storage room. Unrelated and low quality.

photos.conclusion: Of 10 candidate Google Maps photos tied to this business's place_id, only 2 clearly show real handyman work and a 3rd is a borderline maybe. That is below the pipeline's hard minimum of 5 usable real photos (PIPELINE.md Fase 3, point 5). Google Maps photo pools for small/low-traffic listings routinely mix in photos from unrelated check-ins at the same reviewer's other visited places, which appears to be exactly what happened here. This session could not reach Google Maps directly (JS-rendered, blocked to the fetch tools available) to pull a fresh, larger photo set, and Facebook/Yelp/Angi/HomeAdvisor were all blocked (login wall or HTTP 403) to further source real photos.

prior_unfinished_work_found_in_repo.note: A complete but low-quality build already exists here (index.html + content.json), built 2026-11-14, generic/templated copy with no real service or review detail, and it uses gmaps-1.jpg (the unrelated campus sunset photo) as both the brand logo and the og:image. This build was never added to data/processed.json. It should probably be deleted or redone, not used as-is; this session did not touch it.

A deeper research pass (data.json only, no index.html), also 2026-11-14, with the full 14-review Google Maps data and the 10 gmaps photos evaluated above. It looks like that session correctly stopped before building once it hit the same photo problem documented here, and never registered a result either. This session's data.json builds on and supersedes that research.

failure_reason: Fewer than 5 real, verifiably-relevant photos of this business's own work after visual curation (hard minimum per PIPELINE.md Fase 3, point 5). Confirmed no own website, no email, no Instagram; a Facebook page exists but is fully login-gated and could not be inspected. This session exhausted the available research tools (WebSearch budget for this turn, WebFetch against Google Maps/BBB photos page/Angi/HomeAdvisor/Yelp, Facebook login wall, dead historic domain with no reachable Wayback snapshot) without finding a 4th or 5th usable photo. No site was built and no outreach draft was written, per the pipeline's rule that `failed` is reserved for cases below the real-data minimums rather than filling the gap with stock or unrelated imagery.
recommended_next_step_for_a_future_sessi: Retry with a tool that can actually render Google Maps (a browser/computer-use tool) to pull the full photo set directly from the business's own Google Business Profile tab (not the mixed 'all photos at this pin' pool), which usually separates owner-uploaded photos from customer photos and could turn up more usable, unambiguous work photos.
